short: What the owners would be left with after all debts are paid.
metaDescription: Equity is what belongs to the owners: total assets minus total liabilities. Equity is the honest measure of what a business is worth on its own books.
definition: Equity is what belongs to the owners: total assets minus total liabilities. It comprises capital introduced plus accumulated retained earnings, less any drawings or distributions.
bodyHtml:
Why Equity matters

Equity is the honest measure of what a business is worth on its own books. Growing equity means the business is building value rather than merely turning over cash.

Equity formula

Equity = Assets − Liabilities

Also: capital introduced + retained earnings − drawings.

How Equity works in practice

Watch capital introduced separately from retained earnings. A rising equity balance driven only by fresh owner money is a very different story from one driven by profits.

faq.question: Is equity the same as the business's market value?
faq.answer: No. Book equity reflects recorded costs, not what a buyer would pay.

faq.question: What does negative equity mean?
faq.answer: Liabilities exceed assets, usually after accumulated losses — a serious solvency signal.
